keyVerseText: And saith unto him, If thou be the Son of God, cast thyself down: for it is written, He shall give his angels charge concerning thee: and in their hands they shall bear thee up, lest at any time thou dash thy foot against a stone.
rootMeaning: The Greek verb προσκόπτω (proskóptō) originates from the combination of πρός (prós), a preposition indicating direction or contact, and κόπτω (kóptō), meaning to strike or beat. Literally, it conveys the action of striking one thing against another, often implying a direct encounter or collision. This root sense enriches the common English glosses like "stumble" or "dash" by highlighting the physicality and intentionality of the striking or tripping motion, whether literal or figurative.
usageInScripture: Throughout Scripture, προσκόπτω appears eight times with a consistent semantic range involving physical or metaphorical stumbling and striking. It is translated variously as "thou dash," "he stumbleth," "beat upon," and "stumble," reflecting both literal impacts (such as dashing a foot against a stone) and figurative offenses or obstacles. This consistency reveals the word's dual capacity to describe tangible physical missteps and spiritual or moral offenses that cause one to falter.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding προσκόπτω in its original sense deepens our grasp of how Scripture portrays human vulnerability and spiritual challenges. The image of stumbling or being struck against an obstacle underscores the reality of sin and temptation as forces that can cause believers to falter. Yet, it also points to God's protective care, as believers are warned to avoid such pitfalls. Christ, who perfectly resisted stumbling, becomes our model and strength, enabling us to stand firm without offense. This word thus enriches our appreciation for the perseverance and grace necessary in the Christian life.
keyVerseReflection: In Matthew 4:6, the devil tempts Jesus to cast Himself down, warning that angels will prevent Him from dashing His foot against a stone. Here, προσκόπτω vividly captures the danger of a physical stumble, emphasizing the risk of harm even in divine protection. The word highlights the reality of trials and the possibility of faltering, yet also the assurance of God's sovereign care. This verse, through προσκόπτω, invites believers to trust God's providence without testing Him by reckless actions.
